definition: Clever and quick with words in a way that makes people laugh or smile.
example: My grandfather's witty comments at dinner keep everyone laughing between bites.
nuance: Witty humor comes from clever wording and quick thinking, while funny can describe anything that gets a laugh, even a pratfall.
prompt: A student gives a short speech at the class awards night.
options: Her witty remark about the squeaky microphone made the whole audience laugh.
Her witty speech was so flat and humorless that several parents dozed off.
Her witty joke took ten minutes to set up and confused everyone at the end.
She was too witty to speak and simply stared at the floor in silence.
reasons: A quick, clever joke about the moment that wins laughs shows sharp verbal humor.
A dull talk that puts people to sleep is the opposite of clever humor.
The word implies quickness and a joke that lands; a slow, confusing one shows neither.
Silence shows no humor at all; the word does not describe shyness or stage fright.

practice.prompt: Two friends write captions for photos in the school yearbook.
options: Leo's witty caption repeated the same tired joke the class had heard all year.
The witty caption was printed in tiny gray letters along the bottom edge.
Maya wrote a witty caption calling the soggy picnic photo a rain check.
Leo's witty caption simply listed the names of everyone in the photo.
reasons: This kind of humor depends on fresh cleverness; a stale, worn-out joke lacks it.
Font size and color describe how text looks, not whether its words are clever or amusing.
Turning a wet picnic into a clever pun is exactly the kind of playful wordplay meant.
A plain list of names is useful information but contains no cleverness or humor.
